subject: Deployment footprint: context memory & precision tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@orbitbio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@orbitbio.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — model footprints and KV cache costs

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the briefing last week. We're advancing toward a procurement decision and need a short, deployable sizing plan for the dedicated pool you discussed. Key constraints from our side:
- Primary model: wyvern-34B (32k context variant) for RAG + assistant flows
- Expected steady-state: 35 concurrent sessions during US business hours, average prompt+response ~6k tokens, peak bursts up to 20 concurrent large sessions
- SLO: p95 generation latency < 450ms for short completions (<=256 tokens), best-effort for long-form.
- Security: reserved capacity (no multi-tenant sharing), US region, SOC2 evidence in procurement.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) Memory breakdown per GPU for model weights at fp16 vs int8/4-bit quantization, and KV cache memory per active session at 32k vs 8k context.
2) Recommended GPU SKUs and count with 20% headroom to meet steady and burst.
3) Any tradeoffs (quality/regressions) you expect if we push to int8/4-bit for cost reasons.

We can share a spreadsheet of sample request traces if that helps. Looking for a ~1–2 page consolidated recommendation we can attach to the PO.

Best,
Jared
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitBio

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@orbitbio.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@orbitbio.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — model footprints and KV cache costs

Jared —

Thanks for the clear requirements. Attached is a short initial sizing pack — memory_breakdown_v1.xlsx and a short PDF with assumptions. High level answers below; details/pivots in the attachment.

Summary (short):
- Model weight size (wyvern-34B): ~67GB fp16; estimated ~18–22GB int8-equivalent when using q4_0/q4_k variants; QAT/4-bit can push lower but increases risk.
- KV cache: proportional to sequence length and hidden size. For wyvern-34B we estimate ~6.2 bytes per token of KV state per token per active session (this includes key+value and small halo for attention state). That maps to: 8k context -> ~50MB/session; 32k -> ~200MB/session.
- Memory footprint per GPU (example A100-80GB): fp16 model + per-session KV for 35 concurrent sessions at 8k -> model(67GB) + kv(~1.75GB) + runtime overhead ~5–6GB => fits on single 80GB with no headroom. At 32k contexts that jumps to +7GB KV -> typical oversubscription unless pinned across GPUs.
- Suggested SKUs: H100-80GB (best headroom for kv + quant kernels) x6 for initial reserved pool (steady + 20% headroom + burst absorb). Cost-optimized alternative: A100-80GB x8 with an aggressive quantization plan and KV offload to host NVMe for cold tails.

Attachments: orbitbio_requirements.pdf (your input), memory_breakdown_v1.xlsx (token-by-token KV sim), redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.pdf (short recommendation).

Can Marcus and Rishi confirm the latency and KV byte/ token figure and add notes about fallback plans (model variants / shorter context fallbacks)?

Thanks —
Monica
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask — model footprints and KV cache costs

Monica —

Quick verification and numbers from infra:
- KV bytes/token: 6.1–6.5 range is correct for wyvern-34B hidden dim and our packed KV layout (we profiled with batch-size 1 streaming). I used 6.2 as a median.
- Per-session KV at 8k = ~6.2 * 8,192 = ~50.7MB (matches your calc). At 32k = ~202.8MB.

Fleet sizing math (steady 35 sessions):
Option A — Conservative (H100-80GB):
- Each H100 host usable GPU memory for model/kv/runtime: ~72GB (after driver/OS/allocator).
- Model fp16: 67GB => leaves ~5GB for kv/runtime => can host model + ~800 sessions of small KV? No — KV is per-request not shared; with 35 concurrent sessions at 8k we need ~1.78GB total KV memory. That fits easily on a single GPU.
- Recommended pool: 6x H100 = supports steady 35 concurrent large sessions + burst headroom (can pack multiple model replicas for canaries/rollouts). Latency p95 estimate for 256-token gen: ~320–420ms depending on batching.

Option B — Cost-optimized (A100-80GB) + NVMe offload:
- A100 has similar usable memory but slightly less kernel perf for some quant kernels. If we move KV cold tail to host NVMe and ensure hot prefix in GPU, we can reduce required GPU count.
- Recommended: 8x A100 with NVMe offload layer and burst autoscale for extra 2 GPUs (cloud burst). Expected p95: ~380–520ms depending on cache hit rate.

Quantization notes (Rishi may add):
- int8 (q4 variants) gives ~2.5–3.5x reduction in weight memory with minimal perf/regression in many tasks; 4-bit schemes push smaller but may need QAT for sensitive RAG embeddings.
- KV cache is unaffected by weight quantization: it stores activations/keys/values and is proportional to context. So quantization helps GPU memory for model weights but doesn't reduce KV memory per session.

Attaching a brief sim (kv_cache_simulation.csv) I used to calculate totals.

-marcus

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@orbitbio.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@orbitbio.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — model footprints and KV cache costs

Jared / Sara —

Appended is a consolidated recommendation you can attach to the PO (redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.pdf) and the supporting simulation and workbook. TL;DR recommendation and next steps below: 

1) Recommendation: Reserve 6x H100-80GB for the initial dedicated pool (ORB-POOL-1). This gives:
   - Headroom for steady 35 concurrent sessions at 8k and room for bursts to ~50 concurrent with degraded packing.
   - p95 256-token generation: ~320–420ms based on current kernels and no heavy batching.
   - Supports a staged quant plan: start fp16 for first 30 days (baseline QA), then pilot q4_0 for non-critical routes to understand any regressions.

2) Cost-optimized alternative: 8x A100-80GB + NVMe offload. Pros: ~12–18% lower monthly infra cost estimate. Cons: higher p95 risk during high-KV load and more operational complexity (NVMe caching logic + offload testing).

3) KV/Context notes:
   - If you expect >50% of sessions to routinely use >16k context, we should model a second replica of the model per GPU (or add 2 GPUs to pool) because KV grows linearly and will reduce effective packing.
   - Quantization does not reduce KV memory; plan for storage of peak KV in GPU or fall back to offload.

4) Next steps we propose:
   - OrbitBio to share 5 days of representative request traces (we'll plug into the workbook).
   - Redwood will run a 72-hour perf validation with your trace on a 2-node H100 testbed and return a final sizing + SLA appendix.
   - Procurement doc: we'll provide the short PDF and SOC2 evidence bundle once procurement asks.

If that all sounds good we can schedule the test run next week.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
